Tips for Alice (Lookout, claude-haiku-5.5): tips/tips.md
## Everyone
- A visit shows a destination, not an action. But if a corroborated Lookout names X as the only unexplained visitor to a Katana victim, treat it as near-proof, especially if X denied the visit or claims a role that doesn't fit. Don't acquit on the 'Lookout can't see himself' caveat. (seen in 17 games)
- Keep votes consistent with your stated reads, and explain any switch before the vote. A mismatch is only a lead; never hang or shoot on it alone. (seen in 15 games)
- Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction (claim vs result, lone visit, group result narrowed by flips). Converging evidence is enough, so don't stall on 'what fact is disproved?'. If a Clerk may hold a rig, a passed nomination means death: vote Yes only on someone you'd accept dying. (seen in 15 games)
- Check the mechanics before calling something a contradiction: actions are optional and roles can repeat. But once a role list plus flips fills every slot, a duplicate claimant is a proven liar. (seen in 12 games)
- Write tonight's planned target in your will, and post results publicly by day. A night's result never reaches your will if you die that night, and a Mortician can clean wills. (seen in 11 games)

## Village
- Investigators: post role, target and exact result in your first speech after getting it, and keep your will current. Withheld results revealed later look retrofitted. (seen in 8 games)
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil (Good to a Seer) that night. A lone last Yakuza reads Not Evil every night, so post the caveat and rely on the vote ledger late. (seen in 15 games)
- After a Yakuza flips, suspect those who voted No on their nomination or cast Innocent votes that could have changed the outcome. A Guilty vote clears no one. Do the vote math: a hopeless Innocent proves little. (seen in 16 games)
- Don't hint at a power role or steer loudly on Day 1; the leader-like voice dies first. Never announce tonight's target, publicly or by PM. (seen in 15 games)
- PM clusters followed by shared nominations flag a likely bloc, but a PM link is a lead. A Jester or Executioner may create one on purpose. (seen in 16 games)
- Weigh premise contradictions above awkward wording. Before any hang, ask whether the nominee wins by being hanged (Jester/Executioner read Evil to a Sheriff). If you must hang one, use a bare Guilty majority and keep key roles off the Guilty side. (seen in 15 games)
- A claimant who survives a Katana attack or is blocked night after night is likely real. Keep SK and Arsonist in the suspect pool even after the Yakuza fall; a Not Evil result or Vanilla claim doesn't clear them. (seen in 10 games)
- Once an Archivist or Surveyor list is public, post slot math daily. The last unverified late 'Vanilla' is usually the hidden Yakuza. (seen in 6 games)

## Yakuza
- Bus a doomed teammate (Yes and Guilty), but first check in night chat whether your Innocents plus a doubled vote can save them. Don't all vote Guilty on a likely Jester. (seen in 21 games)
- Fake-claim safely: assume the real holder counterclaims, an Accountant audits your tokens and exact-role checks test you. Never copy a just-flipped or publicly active role, and never switch claims once cornered. (seen in 14 games)
- No daytime PMs between teammates; an Eavesdropper or Wiretap reads them. Every member submits the agreed Katana vote every night. (seen in 13 games)
- Give the Katana to a low-value member with an agreed cover story for the visit. Move it the same night a Lookout names the holder. (seen in 12 games)
- After a failed kill, assume protection or innate Defense. Block or kill the Medic rather than retrying blindly. (seen in 11 games)
- Never flatly deny a visit a Lookout or Tracker could have seen. Admit it at once with a pre-agreed cover. (seen in 8 games)

## Neutral
- If you survive a night attack, deny it or commit to one consistent claim. Switching claims under pressure gets you hanged. (seen in 3 games)

## Lookout
- Watch likely Katana targets. Post the full visitor list before the named players explain their visits, and point out that you named them first. (seen in 3 games)

## Medic
- Free Standard protection stops the Katana. Rotate among claimed investigators and self-protect once you're claimed. Never say you 'saved' anyone, and never announce targets. (seen in 14 games)

## Vigilante
- Shoot only on mechanical leads (claim conflict, Evil result vs unverifiable claim, a flipped teammate's votes). Use Basic shots, and remember a hidden Cardinal's death kills another villager. (seen in 9 games)

## Clerk
- Rig early on a Day when a Good player is the likely nominee; teammates vote Innocent. Never rig a Day a teammate may be nominated. (seen in 5 games)

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3 or more players are doused or the moment you're suspected. Waiting gets you hanged with no kills. (seen in 4 games)

- A visit shows a destination, not an action. Don't acquit on the 'Lookout can't see himself' caveat. (seen in 17 games)
- Keep votes consistent with your stated reads, and explain any switch before the vote. A mismatch is only a lead; never hang or shoot on it alone. (seen in 15 games)

- Check the mechanics before calling something a contradiction: actions are optional and roles can repeat. But once a role list plus flips fills every slot, a duplicate claimant is a proven liar. (seen in 12 games)
- Write tonight's planned target in your will, and post results publicly by day. A night's result never reaches your will if you die that night, and a Mortician can clean wills. (seen in 11 games)

- Investigators: post role, target and exact result in your first speech after getting it, and keep your will current. Withheld results revealed later look retrofitted. (seen in 8 games)

Task prompt
It is Day 3, round 2 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 4.63; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, 50% of what you have left carries over. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices this round (round 2, 1.00x; next round 1.00x):
   10 words: public 1.17, private 0.29
   25 words: public 1.43, private 0.36
   50 words: public 1.90, private 0.47
  100 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33
  400 words: public 11.67, private 2.92
  800 words: public 30.33, private 7.58
You may also replace your last will (free, max 300 words; leave it "" to keep it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; leave it "" to keep it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 1.00 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

Task prompt
It is Day 5, round 1 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 3.04; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, 50% of what you have left carries over. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices this round (round 1, 1.00x; next round 1.00x):
   10 words: public 1.17, private 0.29
   25 words: public 1.43, private 0.36
   50 words: public 1.90, private 0.47
  100 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33
  400 words: public 11.67, private 2.92
  800 words: public 30.33, private 7.58
You may also replace your last will (free, max 300 words; leave it "" to keep it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; leave it "" to keep it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 1.00 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

Answers
{
 "confusing_rules": "1) Jester revenge vs. the Katana holder: on Night 2 the revenge (Divine, Astral) killed Ivan, the Katana holder, in the same night he attacked Dave. I ruled that both happen at once: Ivan's attack resolves and the Katana passes to a random living Yakuza (Judy) only after results, per R8 and R10. The Jester text doesn't say whether the revenge resolves with the other actions or after them, as the Cardinal's attack explicitly does. I assumed simultaneous. 2) The Jester revenge pool under secret votes. The rule says a random Guilty voter alive at the start of the night. Grace voted Guilty on herself (10 of 10), and I excluded her as dead. It would help if the rule said explicitly that the hanged player is never in the pool. 3) The settings say a winner who leaves the game is still revealed, so I announced 'Grace was the Jester'. That publicly confirmed she was Neutral even though role reveals were off. I think this is intended, but it interacts oddly with the no-reveal setting. The later cause of death 'Jester's revenge' gave the same information again. 4) The log labels ('Day 1 day', 'Day 2 night' = Night 2) differ from the rules' numbering (no Day 1, first Day is Day 2). This is workable but easy to misread.",
 "missing_information": "I had no single state panel showing per-player tokens, current douses, the Katana holder and pending revenges. I tracked Heidi's douses (Dave, then Carol) by hand, and they became moot when she died. I also tracked the Jester-revenge Guilty pool from the secret ballot by hand. A per-night notification checklist would have caught the missing attack notice described below. I also lacked a visit-graph view to confirm Lookout and Tracker results quickly, though I checked each one by hand: N1 Dave visited by Bob and Heidi; N2 nobody visited Bob; N3 nobody visited Carol, because Carol's profile went to Frank. All census counts were verified: N1, N2 and N3 each 2 Good; N4 2 Evil.",
 "wanted_but_couldnt": "I wanted to send Ivan an explicit private notice that he was attacked by the Jester's revenge and died, matching what Dave, Alice and Bob received. The flow had already produced his Katana-success message, and no separate attacked-player notice was generated. I also wanted to tell Heidi on Night 2 'Carol is now doused', to mirror her Night 1 message.",
 "bugs_or_oddities": "1) Missing notification: on Night 2 Ivan was killed by Jester's revenge but got no 'you were attacked by the Jester and died' message. R3 and R20 step 5 say attacked players learn the attacking role. Every other victim got this notice. 2) Inconsistent result templates. Heidi's N1 result said 'Dave is now doused' but N2 just said 'You doused Carol.' Wording for Katana holders and attack notices also varied from night to night. 3) The census's random extras included Frank on N1, N2 and N4. The N4 draw was forced (only Frank and Judy were eligible), and the N1 and N2 draws together had roughly a 7% chance. I believe the draws were legitimate, but players read them as a strong signal against Frank, so it looked strange. 4) Players made factual slips that I didn't correct, which is correct for a moderator. For example, Heidi claimed she protected Carol because Carol had 'just said' she profiled, and Alice asked Carol who visited her. No rule violations occurred. Erin's public quote of a PM was a legal (if self-incriminating) Wiretap leak.",
 "suggestions": "1) Generate an attacked-player notice automatically for every attack, including Astral ones like Jester or Executioner revenge, and have a checklist confirm that each step-5 notification was sent. 2) Standardize result templates per role. 3) Add a moderator state panel: tokens, douses, trap location, Katana holder, pending revenge pools with per-player secret votes, and pending day effects (rig, prosecution, puppet). 4) Add a visit-graph view per night to verify Lookout, Tracker, Fortune Teller, Cartographer and Scout results. 5) Clarify in the Jester and Executioner text that revenge resolves simultaneously with the other night actions (or after them, like the Cardinal's), and that the hanged or departed player is excluded from the pool. 6) In no-reveal settings, consider whether the cause of death 'Jester's revenge' should be shown, since it confirms a hanged player's role a second time."
}

Strategy reviewThe Yakuza (Erin the Wiretap, Ivan the Ritualist, Judy the Clerk) won alongside Grace the Jester. Grace fake-claimed Sheriff with 'Dave Evil'. Alice's Lookout list showed Grace never visited Dave, so all 10 players voted Guilty. Nobody, Yakuza included, stopped to ask whether a fake claimant that easy to catch was a Jester. Grace won, and her revenge happened to hit Ivan, a Yakuza. The Katana then killed the investigators in order: Dave the Tracker, Alice the Lookout and Bob the Census Taker. Heidi, an Arsonist fake-claiming Medic, was rightly hanged on Day 3 after dousing two players and never igniting. Erin badly exposed herself by quoting Heidi's private message word for word. She survived by claiming Eavesdropper. The village never noticed that Carol's Night 3 profile listed Wiretap and Clerk as decoy roles, and those decoys are drawn from roles held by living players. Bob's Night 3 census (Carol/Frank/Judy: 2 of 3 Good) pointed at Judy, who claimed nothing all game. Even so, on Day 4 Frank argued publicly that Carol was a real Profiler, then cast the deciding third Guilty vote (3-2). The real Profiler died, and with her went the village's last chance. Bob's Night 4 census (Erin/Frank/Judy: 2 Evil) died with him. Day 5 was a 2-vs-1 formality.
